text: You’re walking along, comfortable in your rhythm. Places to be, your personal space bubble moves with you.
Then, it happens. A figure ahead, just slow enough to break your flow. You adjust, hoping for an opening, but they remain an obstacle.
You try a gap, weaving left, then right. Their invisible space expands, blocking your every move. It *always* feels like a cosmic joke.
It's not personal. Everyone has a space bubble. Walk faster, you *catch up* to more slow people. They aren't blocking; just a slower part of the flow.
The cost: you spend far more *time* stuck behind slow movers than *passing* others. Memory amplifies frustrating minutes, forgetting easy moments.
Tomorrow, you’ll walk again. Understand pedestrian flow. Not stuck by bad luck, but the physics of moving bubbles.
